', scripts/build_report.py:143: '

A second independent Athena++ benchmark propagates the actual rotating boundary with B=0, using HLLC/PLM/RK2, the same gravity and thermal closure, and exactly prescribed inner mass flux. Positivity floors are configured to abort rather than conceal failures; none activate. Its 72→96-cell refinement changes the PN-weighted incident flux by −10.47% and the local time series by up to about 24.5%. The in-house hydrodynamic LLF controls also retain substantial method dependence. Thus the outstanding transport sensitivity exists without magnetic cleaning. A smooth hot radial-wind check against the analytic Bernoulli relation gives coarse speed errors of approximately −2.47% for the in-house solver and −0.35% for Athena; these checks do not identify a major pressure-unit or gravity error. Inputs, problem generator, native outputs and comparisons.

', scripts/build_report.py:146: '

The single-precision CUDA branch is separately checked against double precision. On the complete 25-day 96×16×96 global run, maximum incident-flux differences during the pointing are 0.0095%, and the PN mean changes less; the same step and fallback counts are retained. Its solve takes about 97 s versus 244 s in double precision, with 78 versus 156 MB of device arrays. Full coarse split and cone cases also keep precision effects well below the numerical-method discrepancy. The optimized branch changes host/device synchronization only and reproduces saved FP32 fields, probes and rejection statistics exactly in full coarse global, split and CME cases. Measured 96-grid flux kernels take less than 0.25 ms in double precision and less than 0.04 ms in single precision. These timings are subject to shared-device load. Full wide precision check; kernel-duration measurements.

', scripts/build_report.py:148: '

On the balanced 96×32×96 raw-driver grid, HLLE and split LLF differ by at most 0.8% in local incident flux, but contact-resolving HLLD lowers the PN mean from 1.755×10⁸ to 1.497×10⁸ cm⁻² s⁻¹ and changes local flux by up to 28%. HLLD uses a global first-order fallback on 4183 of 21119 accepted steps; on days 32–33 this is 455 of 1633 steps. These historical controls identify contact transport and global fallback as outstanding issues rather than proving agreement among all methods. Interface fallback counters include Riemann evaluations in rejected attempts and have a different denominator from accepted-step fallback counts. daily step histogram; interface fallback reasons.

', scripts/build_report.py:149: '

With the corrected thermodynamic boundary, the same balanced 96 grid gives PN incident flux 1.467×10⁸ cm⁻² s⁻¹, a 2.03% reduction from the raw driver. Halving CFL from 0.35 to 0.175 then raises the PN mean by 4.84% and changes local incident flux by up to 9.41%, failing the registered 1% temporal target. Global fallback affects 20.3% versus 22.0% of accepted steps. This shows that the earlier legacy timestep pass cannot certify the newer contact-resolving calculation. Exact controlled comparison.

', scripts/build_report.py:150: '

A separate conservative local-repair branch addresses that global downgrade. Failed cells seed a union mask; every shared face touching it uses first-order HLLE, while other faces retain MUSCL-HLLD. Both RK stages restart from the conserved backup at the same timestep, with a bounded expansion count and explicit global-fallback escape. No state is clipped. The coarse CPU control needs no global fallback and uses first-order flux on only 0.54% of accepted face evaluations; all nine conserved-variable budgets close to about 10⁻¹⁴ after accounting for boundary flux, gravity and cleaning damping. Exact CPU/CUDA64 controls pass. FP32 proton precision fails on the very coarse 24 grid (maximum 4.13%) but passes on the 48 grid (maximum 0.935% over the full pointing); magnetic and transverse-velocity precision remains worse. Local repair changes the coarse PN flux materially and raises global divergence, so it requires its own production refinement and magnetic diagnostics. Implementation and precision gates; Controlled physical effect.

', scripts/build_report.py:160: '

Latitude-width experiments must be interpreted separately from cell-resolution experiments. The early coarse ±30°/±60° comparison changes flux by approximately 14%; that is measured sensitivity, not a validated ±14% uncertainty bound. Comparisons of different numerical fluxes also need to remain separate from domain comparisons. Exact-GLM preprocessing with the original dissipation changes the coarse PN flux by less than 1%, whereas a split GLM treatment with lower transverse dissipation can change it much more. This numerical-method dependence must not be hidden behind a single successful refinement test. Full divergence and scheme diagnostics; independent domain assessment.

', scripts/build_report.py:161: '

GLM cleaning leaves nonzero magnetic divergence. In the narrow-domain final day-34 snapshots, the comet-neighborhood h|div B|/|B| decreases from about 0.018 on the coarse grid to 0.006 on the medium grid, and the medium nearest-cell value is about 0.003. These are not PN-epoch measurements or diagnostics of the wider fine reference.
